newsitem.title: USA: Chateau approves revised ROC merger.
newsitem.headline: Chateau approves revised ROC merger.

text.p: Chateau Properties Inc said Wednesday its board of directors unanimously approved a revised merger agreement with ROC Communities Inc.
The company said it rejected merger proposals from both Manufactured Home Communities Inc and Sun Communities Inc.

"In reaching its decision, the board determined...that the revised merger agreement with ROC is the best alternative for Chateau stockholders and represents the opportunity for both superior long-term value and strategic and operational benefits," Chateau said in a statement.
In July, ROC and Chateau signed a definitive agreement to merge, but Chateau was then approached by the two other companies. ROC also said it approved the new pact.
Under the revised ROC agreement, each Chateau share will represent 1.0316 shares of the resulting combined company. The exchange ratio for ROC shares is unchanged at 1.042.
Under the revised agreement, ROC would merge with a subsidiary of Chateau, the company said.
In the original agreement shareholders of Chateau common stock were to receive one new share per Chateau share.
The revised merger is subject to the approval of a majority of Chateau common stockholders and two-thirds of the ROC shareholders, Chateau said.

Chateau said ROC shareholders will vote first, and if approved the Chateau operating partnership (OP) unit holders will have the option to exchange, on a tax-efficient basis, the OP units for voting shares before the Chateau vote.

The OP unit holders will be required to waive the right to OP dividends in recognition of the tax-efficent exchange, the company said. Certain OP unit holders intend to exchange some six million units into common stock, Chateau said.
The chairman of the combined company would be John Boll, current chairman of Chateau, and the chief executive officer would be Gary McDaniel, CEO of ROC.
Chateau also said its board approved a stock repurchase plan under which it will buy back up to 1.45 million shares of the 6.1 million currently outstanding.
In addition, Englewood, Colo.-based ROC intends to purchase up to 350,000 shares of Chateau common stock prior to the merger, Chateau said.

Chateau said a class action suit had been filed in Maryland against it on September 12 alleging the directors violated their fiduciary duties by not endorsing the MHC offer. Chateau said it intends to defend against the suit.
Chateau said it filed a suit September 17 in Maryland against MHC in connection with its tender offer, alleging the offer was made in violation of U.S. securities laws.
